::: {.hl-panel .page-head}
# {{< var wrong >}} of {{< var cells >}} boxes were wrong. Here is every one, and why.

That is {{< var wrong_vals >}} wrong values, {{< var invented >}} invented values and {{< var blanks >}} blanks. They fall
into four causes. Each card quotes the document text the AI saw, with the answer key next to the AI's answer. All
documents are [SYNTHETIC](glossary.qmd#synthetic){.gl}.

{{< include _gen/causes.html >}}
:::

::: {.hl-panel .chapter #priority}
## 1. Priority read backwards on new wording ({{< var causes.priority >}} boxes)

The new forms say "P1 - Critical", "P2 - Normal", "P3 - Deferred" or "precedence 2, normal". The AI handled
"P1 - Critical" but turned "normal" into **low**, and once turned "P3 - Deferred" into **high**. All
{{< var causes.priority >}} are on new forms.

{{< include _gen/ex_priority.html >}}

::: {.wtm}
**Why it matters.** A wrong priority can send urgent work to the back of the queue. **Likely fix:** spell out the P1/P2/P3
scale in the AI's instructions, then test on a fresh set of new forms (not these).
:::
:::

::: {.hl-panel .chapter #category}
## 2. "What broke" guessed as engine in free-text notes ({{< var causes.category >}} boxes)

Emails never name the category. The AI has to work it out from a symptom such as "alternator not charging". When unsure,
it tended to answer **engine**: 6 of these 7 wrong answers say engine. On forms and tables, where a label names the
category, it was almost always right.

{{< include _gen/ex_category.html >}}

::: {.wtm}
**Why it matters.** Costs get filed under the wrong system, so reports on what breaks most are skewed. **Likely fix:** give
the AI a short list of example symptoms per category, and send free-text answers to a person for a quick check.
:::
:::

::: {.hl-panel .chapter #date}
## 3. A report date invented when none was given ({{< var causes.date >}} boxes)

Three emails say "came in earlier this week" and give no report date. They do mention the last service date, a decoy
planted on purpose. Twice the AI copied the decoy. Once (doc_014) it wrote 2024-12-11, a date that appears nowhere in the
text. This is the only [hallucination](glossary.qmd#hallucination){.gl} in the run.

{{< include _gen/ex_date.html >}}

::: {.wtm}
**Why it matters.** A believable wrong date is worse than a blank, because nobody notices it. **Likely fix:** make the
checker reject any date that does not appear in the text, so the box stays blank instead.
:::
:::

::: {.hl-panel .chapter #fallback}
## 4. One document fell back to the plain rules ({{< var causes.fallback >}} boxes)

doc_043 writes its date as `19-JUL-2025`. The automatic [checks](glossary.qmd#validation){.gl} want `2025-07-19`. The AI
was shown the error and tried again, twice, and missed the format each time. After three tries the
[fallback](glossary.qmd#fallback){.gl} threw away the whole answer and used the rules, which do not know the new labels.
That cost 5 boxes, 3 of which the AI had actually got right.

{{< include _gen/ex_fallback.html >}}

::: {.wtm}
**Why it matters.** One bad box wiped out good ones. **Likely fix:** convert common date styles in the checker, or keep the
valid boxes and blank only the bad one.
:::
:::

::: {.hl-panel .chapter #numbers}
## What did not go wrong: no made-up numbers

In the {{< var num.cells >}} labor-hours and parts-cost boxes, the AI gave no wrong or invented value. The only misses are
the {{< var num.blank >}} blanks on doc_043. Where a document left the hours or cost out on purpose, it correctly
answered blank.
:::

::: {.hl-panel .chapter #public}
## Real public text: {{< var nhtsa.match >}} of {{< var nhtsa.n >}} vehicle recalls matched NHTSA's own label

[PUBLIC DATA]{.tag .tag-public} The AI read each [NHTSA](glossary.qmd#nhtsa){.gl} recall summary and named the broken
system. NHTSA's own component label is the answer key. In 3 of the {{< var nhtsa.miss >}} misses it named the system that
gets hurt (fuel, brakes) instead of the part that is broken. The {{< var fda.n >}} [FDA](glossary.qmd#fda){.gl} recalls
have no answer key; a hand check agreed on all 10, which is a smoke test, not a measurement.

{{< include _gen/nhtsa.html >}}
:::
